clue.text: Spirit shown by brother Andrew

parts.note: Andy is the usual short form of the name Andrew

explanation.surface: A man named Andrew has a sibling who shows plenty of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a distilled liquor, and liquors are commonly called spirits.

clue.text: Baseball star's two girls

parts.note: Babe is a girl's name or nickname
Ruth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A baseball player turns out to be a pair of young women.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe Ruth was a legendary American baseball player for the New York Yankees.

clue.text: I may appear straight after this character

definitions.text: I may appear straight after this character

parts.words: I may appear straight after this character
parts.note: it reads like someone stepping onstage after another person, but I is the letter that follows a particular letter in the alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor says they will come on right after a certain role.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the letter of the alphabet and the character is a letter, the one that comes just before I.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the spelt-out name of the eighth letter, which comes just before I.

clue.text: Notice old man in study, poker-faced

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first pieces sit within the study

parts.note: a den is a private room for study
an ad, an advertisement, is a notice
pa is informal for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A father sits in the study reading an advert, face giving nothing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadpan means expressionless, just as a poker player keeps an unreadable face.

clue.text: Awfully noble about getting us all together

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of noble are put in a jumbled order

parts.note: C, short for circa, is Latin for about

explanation.surface: A dreadful aristocrat gathers everyone into a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' is the anagram signal, and 'about' gives C for circa. 'getting us' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The French borrowing means as one body, everything at once, which is another way of saying all together.

clue.text: Gets gen about savings

indicators.note: about here means round about, so the letters are turned and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone acquires information about their savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges GETS GEN; gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is money put aside for the future, a sum of savings.

clue.text: Slow-moving girl bringing tray

parts.note: lazy can mean sluggish or slow-moving, as in a lazy river
Susan is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A sluggish young woman carries in a tray.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a revolving serving tray placed in the middle of a table.

clue.text: Initially, come round over voucher

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: O is round in shape
upon means on top of, over

explanation.surface: First call round to hand over a voucher.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a ticket or voucher giving a discount or entitlement.

clue.text: A bishop's pamphlet is hard to understand

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, and the 's supplies an S
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: A churchman's leaflet proves difficult to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract ideas are theoretical and remote from concrete experience, so they are difficult to grasp.

clue.text: All the way, rock band on about hot disc

parts.note: The Who are a British rock band

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cricket word is wrapped round the others

parts.note: the on side in cricket is also called the leg side
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
O is disc-shaped

explanation.surface: A rock group releases a scorching record.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so 'on' gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: To go the whole hog is an idiom for doing something completely, going all the way.

clue.text: Assess greatness at a higher level

parts.note: greatness in the sense of magnitude is size
up means at a higher level

explanation.surface: Judge how great something is from a raised position.
explanation.definitionFit: To size someone up is an idiom for evaluating or forming a judgement of them.

clue.text: Shrewd chief

definitions.meaning: the adjective can mean knowing, sly or cunning
as a prefix-like adjective it means principal

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cunning or knowing and principal or foremost, as in archrival.

clue.text: Specious allegation may bring about stress after start of proceedings

indicators.note: the start of a word means its opening letter is taken

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning
tension is mental or physical stress

explanation.surface: A dubious claim may cause strain once legal proceedings begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' only says the stress comes after P and RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretension is a claim, especially an unjustified one, so a specious allegation fits.

clue.text: Go faster than posse and get free

indicators.note: free suggests letters loosed from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Outrun the posse and escape to freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges the letters of THAN POSSE and GET together.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an idiom for pressing the accelerator pedal, so speeding up.

clue.text: King gets in pinball machine — worth putting in the paper?

indicators.note: gets in means enters, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a pintable is a British name for a pinball machine
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch plays pinball; is that newsworthy?
explanation.definitionFit: Printable means fit to be published, suitable for appearing in a newspaper.

clue.text: Envoy with young woman during New Year?

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece goes inside the other
new suggests a fresh form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A diplomat accompanies a young lady over the New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal on Year, giving EARY, and 'during' places the young woman inside it after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is a person sent on a mission, an envoy.

clue.text: Essentially, a bulletin broadcast about man making a comeback

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram is placed round the other piece
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order
making a comeback means coming back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: In effect, a news report is aired about a man returning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns A BULLETIN into INALLBUTE, which goes 'about' NAM (MAN with 'making a comeback').
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in practice though not officially, which is close to essentially or in effect.

clue.text: Goddess attending feast, Artemis

indicators.note: attending means being present at, so the answer is present within the words

explanation.surface: A goddess turns up at a banquet alongside Artemis.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was a Phoenician goddess of fertility and love.

clue.text: Sup bubbly and bitter with social climber

indicators.note: bubbly suggests fizzing and frothing, so the letters are churned up

parts.note: tart means sour or bitter

explanation.surface: Drink champagne and a sharp beer with a parvenu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' looks like champagne but rearranges SUP into UPS; 'and' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone who has risen suddenly in status and acts arrogantly, a social climber.

clue.text: Girl and boy brought round university yearbook

indicators.note: brought round means wrapped about, so the names surround the other piece

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
Al is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Two youngsters bring a university yearbook.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a book published once a year, a yearbook.

clue.text: Following a visit to the theatre one may be convulsed with laughter

definitions.text: Following a visit to the theatre one may be convulsed with laughter

parts.words: Following a visit to the theatre one may be convulsed with laughter
parts.note: the theatre seems to be a playhouse where a comedy leaves one helpless with mirth, but an operating theatre leaves a patient sewn up

explanation.surface: A night out at a comedy leaves the audience helpless with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is the operating theatre of a hospital, after which a patient has a wound sewn up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means laughing uncontrollably, and literally describes a sutured surgical patient.

clue.text: Examine odd person in suit

definitions.meaning: to ... a place is to look it over before a robbery
an eccentric is informally called a real ...
a suit at law is a legal action brought to court

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers inspecting a target, an eccentric character, and a lawsuit.

clue.text: Deeply distressed, snubbed at college

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub them by ignoring them
up means in residence at university, as at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student felt very hurt after being ignored at university.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' at university when in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut up is a British informal phrase meaning very upset or distressed.

clue.text: Count, more insensitive?

definitions.meaning: comparative of numb, more lacking in feeling

explanation.definitionFit: A number is a count or figure; read as numb plus -er, it means more lacking feeling.

clue.text: Actor, one overacting in Lincs town

parts.note: Cary Grant or Hugh Grant, both film actors
a ham is a performer who overacts

explanation.surface: A performer prone to hamming it up appears in a Lincolnshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincs is the abbreviation for Lincolnshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Grantham is a market town in Lincolnshire, in the East Midlands of England.

clue.text: Told stories about backing German songs

parts.note: to tell stories is to lie, so told stories is lied

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone fibbed in support of some German songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, such as those by Schubert, the plural of Lied.

clue.text: Call on somebody in break-times?

parts.note: a stop is a break or pause
by means times in multiplying, as in two by three

explanation.surface: Visit a friend during your rest periods?
explanation.definitionFit: To stop by is a phrasal verb for paying someone a short visit.
